suppressed.title: Load pets lazily instead of eagerly
suppressed.summary: The `Owner` entity loads its `pets` collection eagerly, which forces pet rows to be fetched whenever an owner is materialized even if the caller only needs owner fields.

suggestion.rationale: This defers loading the pet collection until code actually accesses it, so owner-only reads do not also pull the child rows.
suggestion.equivalenceArgument: This is behavioural, not equivalent: the object graph visible to callers changes from always-initialized pets to on-demand initialization, and lazy access can now raise a loading error outside an active persistence context; the returned rows and columns from the database are not directly changed, but the observable ORM behavior is.
assumptions: Callers that need pets will access them within an active persistence context or via an explicit fetch strategy.
No code depends on pets being initialized immediately after loading an Owner.
suggestion.expectedImpact: Avoids fetching the child collection on owner-only loads; pet rows are read only when needed.

suppressed.title: Load visits lazily and fetch them where needed
suppressed.summary: The eager `visits` collection on `Pet` forces every pet load to pull visit rows even when callers do not use them.

suggestion.rationale: Deferring the collection avoids loading visit rows for pet reads that never touch the association, and the visits can still be fetched explicitly when the UI needs them.
suggestion.equivalenceArgument: This changes when related rows are loaded, so it is behavioural rather than equivalent; the pet row set and columns stay the same, but access to `visits` now happens on demand instead of always being materialized with the pet.
assumptions: Callers that need visits either already access them within an open persistence context or are updated to fetch them explicitly.
The application does not rely on eager initialization side effects during pet loading.
suggestion.expectedImpact: Fewer visit rows are read for pet loads that do not use the association; visit loading moves to the code paths that actually need it.

suppressed.title: Defer loading the specialties collection
suppressed.summary: The eager many-to-many mapping forces specialty rows to be loaded whenever a Vet is fetched, even when the caller only needs the vet itself.

suggestion.rationale: Lazy loading keeps the association from being materialized on every Vet load, so the database only reads the join rows and specialty rows when code actually traverses the collection.
suggestion.equivalenceArgument: This is not equivalent because it changes when the specialties collection is loaded and can change the number and timing of SQL statements, including error behavior for detached entities; the returned Vet rows and columns are the same, but access to specialties is no longer immediate.
assumptions: Callers that need specialties still access the collection inside an active persistence context or explicitly fetch them with a query/entity graph.
The application does not rely on eager loading side effects for serialization or view rendering.
suggestion.expectedImpact: Avoids loading the association for Vet reads that never touch specialties; when specialties are needed, loading is deferred to the access site instead of happening for every Vet query.

evidence.relevance: The mapping eagerly loads a many-to-many association through the join table.
The association is backed by a separate join table, so eager loading necessarily touches additional rows.
